newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk military says rebels shot down helicopters.
newsitem.headline: Turk military says rebels shot down helicopters.

text.p: A spokesman for Turkish military headquarters said on Friday Kurdish rebels had brought down two of its helicopters on a mission in northern Iraq.
"This is the first time two of our helicopters have been shot down," general Erol Ozkasnak told reporters at a news conference broadcast on live television.

Ozkasnak said the rebels of the separatist Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) had used SA-7 missiles to bring down a Cougar troop carrier, with 11 officers and soldiers on board, as well as a second, smaller Super-Cobra attack helicopter.
His comments marked the first public confirmation by the military of PKK claims they had successfully deployed mobile anti-aircraft missiles against Turkish forces.

Thousands of Turkish troops, backed by air power, poured into northern Iraq on May 14 in a cross-border operation against bases of the separatist Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK), fighting for independence or autonomy in eastern Turkey.
Turkish officials say their forces have killed more than 2,000 PKK fighters, a figure Western analysts say is inflated. The PKK puts losses by the army and its Iraqi Kurd allies at almost 800 men.
